title: Redundancy has a capacity cost
hook: Add protected bytes while keeping payload per frame fixed.

doesNotKnow: Separate explicit redundancy cost from its unmodeled reliability benefit.

misconception: Extra protective symbols are free under a fixed communication budget.
objective: Separate explicit redundancy cost from its unmodeled reliability benefit.

claims.text: Redundancy trades transmission capacity for protection against communication errors.
Less redundancy carries {A}; more carries {B}. Every frame spends more of its fixed budget on extra bytes, leaving fewer payload bytes.
Does it hold up? This shows capacity cost only. It supplies no error channel, decoder or evidence that these extra bytes correct errors.
claims.source: {"type":"source-access-hold","note":"No empirical effect or research verdict established. Only bounded arithmetic proposed."}

recall.question: Budget 30 symbols; each frame has 4 payload and 2 checks. How much payload fits?
recall.why: Five whole six-symbol frames carry 20 payload symbols.
